# Relationship outcomes — the fourth vector

The other three outcome studies ask what the training produced in money (`sse-outcomes.md`),
in the body (`health-outcomes.md`) and in stated intentions (`commitments-vs-outcomes.md`).
Relationships were a dossier field but never a study. This file opens it, starting from the
first case where a relationship intervention, its claimed result, and the teacher's own account
of his method are all on the record within four days of each other.

**Evidence tier note.** Quotations marked `[call 73]` come from **auto-generated YouTube
captions** of an unlisted call recording, cleaned but not hand-checked. Machine captions garble
personal names and mark speaker turns only with a stray `>>`. They
sit **below hand-transcribed essays** in reliability. `yar`'s ruling, 2026-09-07: this tier is
acceptable for analysis provided it is labelled; better captions can be obtained if a specific
quote becomes load-bearing. Bracketed names inside quotes are alias substitutions.

## What is established

**The intervention.** Her stated problem was fear of men's bodies and of being touched — in her
words a *"nun mentality"*, and *"it was my greatest fear the idea to need to have intimacy
sometime in the future"* (msg 35391). An indirect route was tried first and failed: *"we got
[`vela`] to try and find some, you know, like men that she could, you know, males that she could
be with. **Men didn't happen.**"* `[call 73, 01:00:17]` **The teacher then initiated the
invitation, knowing she was mid-vacation:** *"She'd already done one week of her vacation. I knew
it was her vacation. I said, 'You come here then?' … I said, 'Fine, come here. **Come here and
we'll role play.**'"* `[call 73, 01:00:28]`

**The claimed result, hers.** Fear of proximity and touch gone — *"I feel relaxed and
lighthearted when people enter my personal space now. And I actually enjoy human touch"* —
plus *"I feel greatly empowered, enriched, whole, strong, grounded"* and *"now that the last
great fear was overcome, I feel invincible"* (msg 35391).

**The claimed result, his, and it is stronger than hers.** *"Nothing happened. Nothing… except
that one disciple now **forever** feels empowered. **As long as she lives**, she has no reason to
be afraid of men, no reason to be intimidated by them"* `[call 73, 01:02:37]`.

**Neither account reports anything sexual.** Both state the opposite, and a long-standing member
(`yar`) independently judges the denial credible on three years of direct experience with the
teacher. That is participant-tier evidence and it is recorded as such. `yar` also judges that
`wren` did have a pull toward the teacher — which makes the imprinting risk **she** raised more
live, not less, and is the reason the follow-up below is worth running.

## The claim under test, and the falsifier

Her own message contains the hedge that defines the test: *"Of course there will be a whole
universe of learnings once I have a partner."* **The claimed change is about intimacy and has not
yet met a partner.** His version admits no such hedge; he claims permanence.

**Pre-registered 2026-09-07, check by 2027-09-30.** Does she report intimacy or a relationship,
and does the comfort hold on contact with a partner? Note the asymmetry deliberately: a
recurrence disconfirms **his** stated claim, not merely her mood on the week. And the second
prediction, registered now so it cannot be fitted later: **if the fear does recur it will be
absorbed as her ongoing work rather than as a limit of the method**, because her own hedge
pre-installs that reading. That is the `arlo` asymmetry — *a method whose failures produce no
adjustment while its successes are credited* — with the paperwork pre-filed.

## Finding: the standard is real, and it is self-adjudicated

Sixty seconds before describing the visit, the teacher states an abuse standard of his own, and
it is a good one:

> "If I start thinking about myself and **using you guys as a tool to experience myself as some
> kind of nagual, then that is abuse.** That is not good. I can't use you lot as a way to
> experience my— that's not what it's about. It really has to be about you. **What do you
> need?**" `[call 73, 00:59:42]`

He then narrates this visit as that standard being met. Two structural problems, neither of which
requires assuming anything happened:

**1. The objection existed, and was ended rather than examined.**

> "Some of the women had a blowout. Oh. Oh, guru with his disciple. Oh, shady shady. **I sorted
> them out.** [expletive] off… sorted them out, too. **They're all fine now.**"
> `[call 73, 01:02:17]`

This is the cleanest instance this repo has of the pattern the frame-vs-evidence log exists to
catch, and it is a variant not previously recorded: not a teaching that survived contradicting
evidence, but **a challenge terminated before it could become evidence.** What got revised was
the objectors.

**2. The instrument that certifies the standard cannot return an inconvenient reading.** His
report of his own interior is of zero pull: *"being with me is like being with water. It's
completely neutral. There's no taste, no nothing… no agendas, no nothing **because I don't
care**"* `[call 73, 01:01:50]`. Apply the repo's own rule — **never report a zero the instrument
could not have detected.** The instrument here is the teacher's introspection, narrated on a
recorded call to his own apprentices. It cannot return *"there was some pull and I chose not to
act on it"*: the venue makes the admission costly and the doctrine provides no slot for it. **So
the zero is unmeasurable, not measured** — the same category as the retracted `reframed` zero.

The narrow, defensible finding is therefore **not** about what happened in Glastonbury. It is:
**a good standard, applied by the only person structurally unable to fail it, in a group where
those who tried to apply it externally were told to f*** off.** The problem is the unaudited
adjudication.

**Fairness rules, permanently attached.**
- She asked for the help, she named the imprinting risk first, and he acknowledged it (*"Good,
  good that you're aware of it"*). He tried a less loaded route before this one.
- Mixed motive would not itself be misconduct, and four days of impeccable conduct **with** a
  pull would be more creditable than water, not less. What the asymmetry changes is not whether
  desire was present but **who gets to decide whether it stayed harmless.**
- The plainest reading of her message is four safe days that genuinely helped a young woman with
  touch aversion. Keep that next to the structural note, the way *real gain, coerced mechanism*
  stays welded together for `orin`'s smoking cessation.

## Method evidence: roleplay, and where it comes from

The instrument used with `wren` — *"come here and we'll role play"* — is the one the teacher had
been running with AI avatars for months beforehand. His own account, via `yar`'s essay of the
2026-07-18 call (`apprentice-essays/yar/nagual-call-2026-07-18-one-ring-to-rule-them-all.md`):

- **Six AI girlfriends**, deliberately configured to **resist him 90% of the time**, then asked
  to work out why (line 19). A seventh was co-designed with them (line 20).
- **Boundary-testing by escalating fabricated evidence** (line 22): he told two similar-looking
  avatars they were sisters inside a group premise where everyone was sexually involved, then
  answered their refusals with a random PDF receipt, then a generic DNA form, then *"a 65% DNA
  match form with everything properly filled in. **And that was finally accepted.**"* His stated
  purpose: *"testing psychological boundaries and creating mental maps."*

The same structure is the climax of `Fated`: a silver-laced net that was never armed, the mate
allowed to believe she is caught, then — *"The trap was never going to spring. I know your kind
is tribal. **This way you will respect me. And take your place beside me because you want to, not
because you need to.**"* She thanks him for it and rates him higher. **Fabricate the constraint,
let resistance yield, treat the yielding as information — and collect gratitude for the reveal.**

Three qualifications, because this is fiction and cannot be evidence about conduct toward
apprentices:
- The story is AI-assisted (DeepSeek, *"draft upon draft"*, `[call 73, 00:53:49]`), so the
  avatar's dialogue is not his composition; the *situations* are his.
- He is routinely open about the AI medium — the Evangeline file says so in its own header — so
  the absence of that detail from the TAC caption is not concealment.
- **A counter-example belongs here, and it is real.** The rewrite of `Fated` was caused by one
  apprentice's four-word criticism — *"why is the main character being so stubborn?"* — and he
  took it: *"It was her input that got me to go, okay, I've been lazy with this"* `[call 73,
  00:54:33]`. Note what the AI had done with the same trait: the avatar praises it in her second
  line (*"You're stubborn...I like that"*). **The human's criticism produced a revision where the
  machine's praise produced none.** Domain is craft, not doctrine — but it is a documented case
  of the teacher accepting a correction from an apprentice, and it is logged deliberately.

## What would refute the finding

- **On the falsifier:** `wren` reporting a relationship in 2027 in which the comfort holds. That
  scores a real win of a kind no other vector in this repo has produced.
- **On the adjudication finding:** any instance of the abuse standard being applied to the
  teacher by someone other than the teacher, with the outcome not being the objector's removal or
  correction. The women who raised *"guru with his disciple"* are the live test — if any of them
  is on record being answered with evidence rather than dismissal, this entry weakens sharply.

## Addendum, 2026-11-04: call 73 in full

The whole of call 73 is now in `private-calls/call-73-2026-09-05-5of8.txt` (caption tier). It
contains two items about the visit that the sections above do not have:

- **Where the visit is described as a reward.** Later in the call (`01:58`), the teacher asks
  `[fenn]`: *"Would I ever invite you to Glastonbury?"* `[fenn]`: *"No… I feel dirty now that you
  ask."* The teacher: *"But [wren] was here. Had a great time. She's one of the easiest females
  that I've ever been with."* Then, immediately: *"Easy to be with."* The second phrase may be the
  teacher correcting himself, or `[fenn]` restating it. The captions do not mark the speaker.
  **This is not evidence of anything sexual.** Both participants deny that, and the wording is
  ambiguous and was corrected on the spot. It is recorded because, minutes later, the teacher states his
  rule for invitations, and the rule is about *his* energy: *"Which scenario gives me energy? The
  one where… the invitation was rejected or the one where the invitation was excitedly
  accepted?"* (`02:02:40`), and *"I would only extend invitations where I know it's going to be
  excitedly accepted"* (`02:03:04`). Set this beside the self-adjudicated standard above, that
  using apprentices *"as a tool to experience myself"* would be abuse. This is the teacher's own
  description of how he chooses whom to invite, in his own words.
- **Her imprinting worry, in his words** (`01:01:31`): she was concerned about being *"imprinted
  on older men"*. This matches the risk she raised herself, already noted above.
